messages:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for release v2.3 -> region: us-west (canary pool: 10%). rolling out now, target group: text-gen models. ps: monitor health checks and 5xx thresholds.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary health checks failing (service=text-gen, env=canary). 5xx rate = 3.8% over last 2m, abort criteria = 2% for 5m. Paging on-call.

alex: I'm oncall. joining. where's the rollout id? @jamie can you paste the deploy id?

jamie: rollout id: r-2026-03-11-331. started at 1790604300. rolling to canary instances: cg-42..cg-51.

priya: quick check: logs show upstream 502 from model-hosts, connection reset in the generator worker. extracting snippets now.

priya: ```
[2026-03-11T18:12:10Z] gen-worker-45 ERROR upstream request failed: POST /v1/generate 502 Bad Gateway (read tcp 10.2.3.45:49912->10.2.9.12:8080: connection reset by peer)
[2026-03-11T18:12:17Z] gen-worker-46 ERROR kv-cache miss heavy, cpu>85% on host
```

alex: metric dashboard: error_ratio(canary)=6.1% over 3m, p95 latency up from 220ms to 720ms. CPU on the canary pool trending up. Looks like backpressure causing retries -> 5xx.

jamie: ack. abort criteria already breached. planning runbook step: enable canary abort flag and trigger rollback. anyone see partial customer impact? @marta?

marta: CS seeing 2 tickets mentioning failures to generate summaries for some users (two enterprise customers). Estimated affected sessions ~120 in last 10m, mostly EU region. I've posted a proactive note to the affected customer list and linked status page.

alex: before flipping flag, confirm command to toggle kill switch: internal feature-store cli -> `ff toggle canary_abort_v2_3 --on` right?

jamie: yes. internal console also has a toggle. I'll flip in 30s, will post command output.

jamie: @deploy-bot initiating feature flag toggle now.

deploy-bot: Feature flag change: `canary_abort_v2_3` set to `true` by jamie (ui). Change propagated to the control plane (3 of 3 replicas) at 18:14:05Z.

alex: good. now triggering automated rollback per rollout policy (policy: abort->rollback-to-stable).
\
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: rollback id rb-2026-03-11-58. Targeting canary instances for drain + replace with stable model variant. Starting controlled drain.

kevin: draining canary pool, scaling down canary instances by 100% over 60s. watch pods: `kubectl get pods -l rollout=r-2026-03-11-331 -w`.

priya: health checks after toggle/rollback: error_ratio -> 0.8% over last 1m, p95 latency down to 240ms. I'm tailing logs, still seeing a few retries but trending down.

jamie: confirmed: rollback completed on canary group at 18:15:12Z (1790604512). control plane reports stable variant in serving path.

incident-bot: NOTE: Abort criteria triggered and rollback executed automatically per policy. Incident severity: S2 (partial customer impact). Pages: 1 active, 0 escalated.

marta: status update published to status.redwood.ai/incident/1790604321. Message: "We observed elevated error rates during a canary rollout that affected a subset of customers; rollback completed and service is stabilizing. Support team is following up with impacted customers." Sent to affected customers list.

alex: handing off to night on-call: @oncall-night. Checklist: verify error_ratio < 1% for 15m, confirm no lingering resource pressure, capture metrics snapshot, save logs for postmortem. I'm adding notes to the incident document.

oncall-night: ack. will monitor for next 4 hours and keep updates in the incident doc. if we see >2% for >5m or new alerts, will escalate to SRE lead.

kevin: small followup: root cause hypothesis — model-host autoscaling reacted slowly under burst, causing connection queuing and upstream resets. We saw high KV-cache miss rates that amplified load. Recommend adding additional canary capacity headroom and toggling smarter ramp policy.

jamie: agreed. action items: (1) postmortem + metrics, (2) tweak canary ramp from linear 10%->50% to stepped with 5min waits, (3) add circuit-breaker to backoff model-server retries when upstream 5xx > threshold. I'll own #2 and #3.

priya: saved logs and grep outputs to the incident doc: artifacts/1790604321/logs.tar.gz. perf traces attached.

marta: CS: I've scheduled customer follow-ups and will include a brief timeline. marking the incident as 'stabilized' on the status page.

alex: closing on-call handover notes. postmortem owners: jamie (deploy pattern), priya (logs/diagnosis), marta (customer comms). Will run a blameless postmortem tomorrow 11:00 PST.

incident-bot: Incident 1790604321 -> STABILIZED. Metrics returning to baseline. Postmortem scheduled. :white_check_mark:
